answer_text:
Let

\[
G=D\alpha^{tr}D\alpha.
\]

The matrix has block form

\[
G=
\begin{bmatrix}
r^2 & 0\\
0 & B
\end{bmatrix},
\]

where \(B\) is the \((n-1)\times (n-1)\) block with entries

\[
B_{ij}=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{x_i^2}{r^2}+1, & i=j,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{x_i x_j}{r^2}, & i\neq j,
\end{cases}
\qquad i,j\in\{3,\dots,n+1\}.
\]

Let

\[
x=(x_3,x_4,\dots,x_{n+1})^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}.
\]

Then

\[
B=I_{n-1}+\frac{1}{r^2}xx^T.
\]

Using the matrix determinant lemma,

\[
\det(I_{n-1}+cxx^T)=1+c\,x^Tx,
\]

we get

\[
\det(B)=1+\frac{\|x\|^2}{r^2}
=1+\frac{x_3^2+x_4^2+\cdots+x_{n+1}^2}{r^2}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\det(G)=r^2\det(B)
=r^2\left(1+\frac{x_3^2+\cdots+x_{n+1}^2}{r^2}\right)
=r^2+x_3^2+\cdots+x_{n+1}^2.
\]

Since the parametrization is on the sphere \(S^n(a)\), the coordinates satisfy

\[
r^2+x_3^2+\cdots+x_{n+1}^2=a^2.
\]

Hence

\[
\det(D\alpha^{tr}D\alpha)=a^2.
\]

So the determinant is indeed

\[
\boxed{a^2}
\]
